label: What Compy found

door.sub: A game running badly or crashing? Compy can look at what changed on this PC.

firstLook.lead: Compy has no earlier sessions to compare with yet, but it can look at what changed on this PC.
firstLook.leadElsewhere: Pick a game, or the whole PC, and say when it started. Compy will look at what changed on this PC.
firstLook.looking: Looking at what changed on this PC…
firstLook.title: What Compy found on this PC

told.title: What you told Compy
told.today: You said it started today. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.thisWeek: You said it started this week. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.thisMonth: You said it started this month. Compy looked back to {{from}}, in case a change came just before you noticed.
told.always: You said it has always been like this.
told.dontKnow: You didn't say when it started, so Compy looked at the last 30 days, back to {{from}}.

firstLook.alwaysBody: Changes made recently came after it started, so Compy didn't list them.

group.looksOff: What looks off on this PC
group.looksOffNote: Compy read these on this PC just now. It hasn't measured whether any of them changes how a game runs.

change.gpuInstalled: Windows installed {{adapter}} {{to}} on {{when}}. Compy can't see which version it replaced.
change.gpuInstalledBare: Windows recorded a {{adapter}} install on {{when}}. Compy can't see which version it replaced.
change.otherDrivers_one: Windows installed or updated {{count}} other driver ({{classes}}), the latest on {{when}}.
change.otherDrivers_other: Windows installed or updated {{count}} other drivers ({{classes}}), the latest on {{when}}.
change.programs_one: {{count}} program was installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}}.
change.programs_other: {{count}} programs were installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}}.
change.programsMore: {{count}} programs were installed or updated on {{day}}: {{names}} and {{more}} more.
change.updatesMinor: Windows also installed security definition updates ({{n}}) and Store app updates ({{m}}). They are counted here, not listed.
change.updatesUnclassified_one: Windows installed {{count}} update that Compy couldn't classify.
change.updatesUnclassified_other: Windows installed {{count}} updates that Compy couldn't classify.
change.displayOther_one: A display driver ({{count}}) was installed or updated, the latest on {{when}}.
change.displayOther_other: Display drivers ({{count}}) were installed or updated, the latest on {{when}}.
change.gameFiles: Steam changed {{game}}'s files on {{when}}. That can be an update, a file check or added content.
change.gameFilesPending: Steam also shows a newer version of {{game}} that isn't installed yet.
change.modUnknownOn: Compy can't tell whether it is turned on.
change.gameFilesSince: Steam hasn't recorded a change to {{game}}'s files since {{when}}.

how.gpuDriver: To see it: Device Manager, Display adapters, your card, Driver tab. Windows can roll a driver back there if it kept the earlier one.
how.windowsUpdate: To see them: Settings, Windows Update, Update history. Some updates can be uninstalled from that page.
how.programs: To see them: Settings, Apps, Installed apps. Windows keeps one date per program, and some programs refresh it when they update themselves.
how.otherDrivers: To see them: Device Manager shows each device's driver version on its Driver tab.

none.gpuDriver: Windows recorded no graphics driver version change in this period.
none.windowsUpdate: Windows Update recorded no monthly Windows update, Windows version update or driver update in this period.
none.windowsUpdateDriverNoEntry: Windows Update recorded no monthly Windows update, Windows version update or driver update in this period; its record has no entry for the graphics driver change on {{when}}.
none.windowsUpdateDriversNoEntry: Windows Update recorded no monthly Windows update, Windows version update or driver update in this period; its record has no entry for any of the {{n}} graphics driver changes.
none.programs: No program shows an install or update date in this period.

firstLook.nothing: Compy found no dated change in this period. That doesn't mean nothing is wrong: Compy hasn't measured how any game runs.
firstLook.unread: Compy couldn't read everything for this period, so it can't say that nothing changed. What it couldn't see is listed below.

limit.title: What Compy couldn't see
limit.classes: Compy reads graphics, audio, network and chipset driver installs only, not other drivers.
limit.noInstallDate: Compy can't see Store apps, or programs that don't record an install date ({{n}} here).
limit.gameNotPicked: Compy didn't look at any game's files, because no game was picked.

why.accessDenied: Windows needs administrator rights to show that log
why.logEmpty: that Windows log is empty or switched off
why.logMissing: this PC has no such Windows log
why.recordsUnreadable: Windows returned {{n}} records Compy couldn't read
why.registry: the list of installed programs couldn't be opened
why.notRead: Compy didn't look it up for this answer
why.tookTooLong: reading took too long, so Compy went on without it
why.partialTimedOut: reading ran out of time, so only the newest records were read
why.partialRowCap: the log holds more records than Compy reads, so older ones are missing
why.partialOutputCapped: the log was too long to read in full
why.partialCoverage: Windows' log only goes back to {{from}}
why.notSteam: this game isn't in a Steam library Compy could read
why.steamUnreadable: Steam's library files couldn't be read
why.steamNoRecord: none of the Steam libraries Compy could read has a record of it
why.steamNoTime: Steam's record has no usable date for when the files changed

limit.steamNewestOnly: Steam keeps only the latest date its files changed for {{game}}, so an earlier change in this period wouldn't show.
limit.hardwareNotReady: Compy is still reading this PC's hardware.
limit.historyUnreadable: Compy couldn't read its own change history.
limit.modsPartialOther: Whether {{game}}'s folder has other graphics mods (only part of the folder was scanned)
limit.modsReaderFailed: Whether {{game}}'s folder has a graphics mod (the reader stopped unexpectedly)
limit.crashesReaderFailed: Whether {{game}} has closed unexpectedly before (the reader stopped unexpectedly)
limit.crashesNoFolder: Whether {{game}} has closed unexpectedly before (Compy couldn't match the game to an install folder)
limit.gameLocation: Compy doesn't know where {{game}} is installed, so it couldn't check its drive or folder.

cantTell.title: What Compy can't tell yet
cantTell.body: Compy hasn't seen a game run yet, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.measure: Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.bodyFew: Compy hasn't got enough sessions of {{game}} yet, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.noneOfGame: Compy hasn't recorded a session of {{game}} yet, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.recorded_one: Compy has recorded {{count}} session of {{game}}. This list shows what changed on this PC; it doesn't compare those sessions, so it can't say here which of these changes matters.
cantTell.recorded_other: Compy has recorded {{count}} sessions of {{game}}. This list shows what changed on this PC; it doesn't compare those sessions, so it can't say here which of these changes matters.
cantTell.pcRecorded_one: Compy has recorded {{count}} game session, but this list is for the whole PC, not one game, so it doesn't compare it with anything.
cantTell.pcRecorded_other: Compy has recorded {{count}} game sessions, but this list is for the whole PC, not one game, so it doesn't compare any of them.
cantTell.unreadGame: Compy couldn't read the sessions it recorded just now, so it can't tell whether {{game}} runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.unreadPc: Compy couldn't read the sessions it recorded just now, so it can't tell whether anything runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.
cantTell.unmatched: None of the sessions Compy has recorded is named {{game}}, so it can't tell whether it runs worse than before, or which of these changes matters.

firstLook.footer: Compy lists what it can see on this PC. It doesn't say why a game runs badly until it has measured it.

measured.lead: Compy has too few sessions of {{game}} to compare yet ({{have}} of {{need}}).
measured.scope: This list is for the whole PC, not one game.

firstLook.privacy: Compy reads this on your PC. It doesn't save it or send it anywhere, and it doesn't save what you tap.

game.title: Which game?
game.other: Another game, or the whole PC
game.loadingSteam: Looking for your installed Steam games…
game.steamUnread: Compy couldn't read your Steam library.
game.steamPartial: Compy read only part of your Steam library, so some games may be missing.
game.chosenWhole: Looking at the whole PC, not one game.

crash.none: Windows has no crash record for {{game}} in the records Compy read.
crash.signatureWhat: the earliest change with an exact time under “{{touch}}” or “{{compy}}” ({{date}}, {{kind}})
crash.signatureWhatNoKind: the earliest change with an exact time under “{{touch}}” or “{{compy}}” ({{date}})
crash.splitWhat: the earliest change with an exact time under “{{touch}}” or “{{compy}}”: {{kind}}
crash.splitWhatNoKind: the earliest change with an exact time under “{{touch}}” or “{{compy}}”

split.both_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} ({{what}}) and at least {{after}} from after.
split.both_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} ({{what}}) and at least {{after}} from after.
split.beforeOnly_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} ({{what}}) and none from after.
split.beforeOnly_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} ({{what}}) and none from after.
split.afterOnly: Of the crash records Compy could read, none are from before {{date}} ({{what}}) and at least {{count}} from after. That is a count by date; Compy hasn't tested whether that change matters to the game.
split.beforeUnread_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from before {{date}} ({{what}}). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say whether any came after.
split.beforeUnread_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from before {{date}} ({{what}}). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say whether any came after.
split.startsLater_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from after {{date}} ({{what}}). The oldest record it could read is from {{oldest}}, so it can't say how many came before. Windows keeps only a limited number of crash records.
split.startsLater_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from after {{date}} ({{what}}). The oldest record it could read is from {{oldest}}, so it can't say how many came before. Windows keeps only a limited number of crash records.
split.startsLaterNoOldest_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from after {{date}} ({{what}}). It can't say how many came before.
split.startsLaterNoOldest_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from after {{date}} ({{what}}). It can't say how many came before.
split.unread_one: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} is from after {{date}} ({{what}}). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say how many came before.
split.unread_other: Of the crash records Compy could read, at least {{count}} are from after {{date}} ({{what}}). Some records couldn't be read, so it can't say how many came before.

running.title: Running right now
running.none: Compy didn't find any program from its list running right now. The list is short and matches by program name only; it holds some recorders and overlays, voice chat apps, launchers, browsers, build and developer tools, and Windows Update.
running.nowGame: This is what is running now, not what was running when the problem with {{game}} happened. Compy didn't see that, and it hasn't measured whether any of these affects a game.
running.nowPc: This is what is running now, not what was running when the problem happened. Compy didn't see that, and it hasn't measured whether any of these affects a game.
running.unread: Compy couldn't read the list of running programs, so it can't say what is running.
running.tookTooLong: Compy didn't finish reading the running programs in time, so it can't say what is running.
running.readerFailed: Compy couldn't read the running programs (the reader stopped unexpectedly).

compy.undone: Compy changed “{{title}}” on {{when}}, and it was undone on {{undone}}.
compy.undoneNoDate: Compy changed “{{title}}” on {{when}}, and it has since been undone.

fact.memorySpeed: Your memory is running at {{now}} MHz; your PC's firmware lists it as capable of {{rated}} MHz.
fact.memoryOneStick: Your PC has 1 memory module, so memory runs in single-channel.
fact.memoryOneChannel: Your {{n}} memory modules all report the same memory channel, so they share one channel.
fact.driveHealth: Windows reports the health of {{drive}} as {{health}}.
fact.gameOnHdd: {{game}} is installed on drive {{drive}}:, which is a hard disk (HDD).
fact.gpuDriverAge_one: Your graphics driver is dated {{date}}, {{count}} day ago.
fact.gpuDriverAge_other: Your graphics driver is dated {{date}}, {{count}} days ago.
fact.freesyncOff: Your AMD graphics card reports FreeSync as off.
fact.onBattery: This PC is running on battery.

factHow.monitorRefresh: To check: Settings, System, Display, Advanced display shows the refresh rate and the ones the monitor supports.
factHow.memorySpeed: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Memory shows the speed it is running at.
factHow.memoryChannels: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Memory shows how many memory slots are used.
factHow.driveHealth: To check: Settings, System, Storage, Advanced storage settings, Disks & volumes shows each drive's health.
factHow.gameOnHdd: To check: Task Manager, Performance, Disk shows whether each drive is an HDD or an SSD.
factHow.gpuDriverAge: To check: Device Manager, Display adapters, your card, Driver tab shows the driver date.
factHow.freesyncOff: To check: AMD Software, Gaming, Display shows the FreeSync setting.
factHow.onBattery: To check: the battery icon in the taskbar shows whether the charger is connected.
factHow.gameDriveFull: To check: Settings, System, Storage shows the free space on each drive.

door.sub: Compy looks at what changed and tells you what it finds.
door.failed: Compy couldn't read its records just now. Nothing on your PC was changed.
door.stillChecking: Compy is still checking. Try again in a moment.

problem.body_one: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last session they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.body_other: In a normal session, {{game}}'s dips stay at about {{beforePct}}% of its average frame rate. In your last {{count}} sessions they fell to about {{nowPct}}%.
problem.spikes: The slowest 1 in 100 frames took about {{nowMs}} ms, against about {{beforeMs}} ms in your normal sessions.
problem.average: It also averaged {{nowFps}} frames per second, against about {{beforeFps}} before.
problem.otherGames: {{games}} also had rough sessions in the same period.
problem.partial_one: Compy also saw 1 more session it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.partial_other: Compy also saw {{count}} more sessions it only measured part of, and what it measured looked rough. A partly measured session never counts on its own.
problem.sinceLasted_one: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} session so far.
problem.sinceLasted_other: It last ran normally on {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} sessions so far.
problem.earlier: It also ran rough {{from}}–{{to}} and recovered.
problem.sinceLastedFull_one: Its last fully measured normal session was {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} session so far.
problem.sinceLastedFull_other: Its last fully measured normal session was {{date}}. The rough run has lasted {{count}} sessions so far.
problem.title_one: {{game}} ran much rougher than usual in its last session
problem.title_other: {{game}} has been running much rougher than usual
problem.oneSession: One session isn't much to go on. If the next one is normal, this may have been a one-off.
problem.mixed_one: 1 session ({{dates}}) may contain two games, so Compy didn't judge it.
problem.mixed_other: {{count}} sessions ({{dates}}) may contain two games, so Compy didn't judge them.

answer.mechanism: Often causes this (not measured on your PC)

backgroundLoad.what: Other programs started while you played

backgroundLoad.openNearby_other: Programs were open when you started; programs were seen starting in other sessions
backgroundLoad.nearby_one: Other programs were seen starting in another recent session
backgroundLoad.nearby_other: Other programs were seen starting in other recent sessions

settingDrift.appliedRestored: A setting Compy applied went off, then came back on

evidence.driverChanged: Your graphics driver changed from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.sessionsSplit_one: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; the rough one used the new one.
evidence.sessionsSplit_other: {{game}}'s last normal session ({{date}}) used the old driver; all {{count}} rough ones used the new one.
evidence.crossGame: {{games}} also got much rougher after the update, and never before it.
evidence.installTimeNotRead: Compy didn't read the exact install time; it saw the new version on {{when}}.
evidence.loadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy your PC was in these sessions.
evidence.figureScope: This figure covers everything except the game, including Compy and Windows itself.
evidence.openCounts_one: It was open in {{r}} of {{rm}} rough session and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCounts_other: It was open in {{r}} of {{rm}} rough sessions and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCountsNamed_one: {{name}} was open at the start of {{r}} of {{rm}} rough session and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.openCountsNamed_other: {{name}} was open at the start of {{r}} of {{rm}} rough sessions and {{n}} of {{nm}} normal ones.
evidence.ramPeak_one: Memory was nearly full (at least {{percent}}% of what's usable) in the rough session that has a memory record: it peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable on {{dates}}.
evidence.ramPeak_other: Memory was nearly full (at least {{percent}}% of what's usable) in {{full}} of the {{count}} rough sessions that have a memory record; the highest peak was {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable ({{dates}}).
evidence.ramNormalRange_one: In {{count}} other rough session, memory peaked no higher than in your normal sessions ({{basePeakGb}} GB).
evidence.ramNormalRange_other: In {{count}} other rough sessions, memory peaked no higher than in your normal sessions ({{basePeakGb}} GB).
evidence.ramUnrecorded_one: {{count}} rough session has no memory record.
evidence.ramUnrecorded_other: {{count}} rough sessions have no memory record.
evidence.ramBaseline: Your normal sessions peaked at {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.ramWarning: Compy saw memory nearly full during that session.
evidence.ramLower: Other rough sessions only reached {{peakGb}} GB.
evidence.ramSinceSingle: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}; the rough session peaked at {{roughGb}} GB.
evidence.ramSince: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}; the highest peak Compy read in the rough sessions was {{roughGb}} GB.
evidence.ramSinceTotalsSingle: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}; the rough session peaked at {{roughGb}} of {{roughTotalGb}} GB usable.
evidence.ramSinceTotals: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}; the highest peak Compy read in the rough sessions was {{roughGb}} of {{roughTotalGb}} GB usable.
evidence.ramSinceFull: Memory was nearly full again in your {{game}} session on {{date}}: it peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable.
evidence.ramSinceLowerClearSingle: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}, against {{roughGb}} GB in the rough session, and the {{date}} session ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.ramSinceLowerClear: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}, against {{roughGb}} GB, the highest peak Compy read in the rough sessions, and that session ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.ramSinceLowerClearTotalsSingle: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}, against {{roughGb}} of {{roughTotalGb}} GB usable in the rough session, and the {{date}} session ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.ramSinceLowerClearTotals: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable in your {{game}} session on {{date}}, against {{roughGb}} of {{roughTotalGb}} GB usable, the highest peak Compy read in the rough sessions, and that session ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.ramSinceFullClear: Memory was nearly full again in your {{game}} session on {{date}} (it peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable), and that session ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.ramSinceUnread: Compy has no memory reading for your {{game}} session on {{date}}.
evidence.driftApplied: Compy's own check found a setting it applied is no longer on.
evidence.driftPower: Compy noticed the power plan is now one Windows designed to save power.
evidence.driftAppliedNamed_one: Compy's own check found that “{{titles}}”, a setting Compy applied, is no longer on.
evidence.driftAppliedNamed_other: Compy's own check found a setting it applied was no longer on. Off now: {{titles}}.
evidence.driftSeenThenOff: Compy last saw it on at {{seen}} and noticed it off at {{noticed}}.
evidence.driftSeenThenChanged: Compy last saw it unchanged at {{seen}} and noticed the change at {{noticed}}.
evidence.driftOther: Compy noticed a setting it watches had changed.
evidence.driftOtherNamed: Compy noticed a setting it watches had changed: {{what}}.
evidence.driftRestored: Compy found it off on {{noticed}}. It was back on by {{restored}}.
evidence.driftRestoredNamed_one: Compy found {{titles}}. It was back on by {{restored}}.
evidence.driftRestoredNamed_other: Compy found these off: {{titles}}. They were back on by {{restored}}.
evidence.driftRestoredNone: No {{game}} session has been recorded since it was back on.
evidence.driftRestoredUnjudged_one: {{count}} {{game}} session has been recorded since it was back on, but it was too short, or Compy couldn't measure enough of it, so Compy didn't judge it.
evidence.driftRestoredUnjudged_other: {{count}} {{game}} sessions have been recorded since it was back on, but each was too short, or Compy couldn't measure enough of it, so Compy didn't judge them.
evidence.driftRestoredRough_one: After it was back on ({{restored}}), {{game}} still ran rough on {{date}}.
evidence.driftRestoredRough_other: After it was back on ({{restored}}), {{game}} still ran rough in {{count}} sessions, the first on {{date}}.
evidence.driftRestoredClear: After it was back on, {{game}}'s session on {{date}} ran in its usual range. One session so far; Compy says a game is back in its usual range after two.
evidence.driftRestoredBetween_one: One {{game}} session since it was back on was measured well enough to read, and it wasn't clearly in its usual range, so Compy can't tell yet.
evidence.driftRestoredBetween_other: Of the {{game}} sessions since it was back on, at least one wasn't clearly in its usual range, so Compy can't tell yet.
evidence.driftRestoredClearUnjudged_one: After it was back on, {{game}} ran in its usual range in {{n}} sessions, the latest on {{date}}. The session after that was too short, or Compy couldn't measure enough of it, so Compy can't say {{game}} is back in its usual range yet.
evidence.driftRestoredClearUnjudged_other: After it was back on, {{game}} ran in its usual range in {{n}} sessions, the latest on {{date}}. Each session after that was too short, or Compy couldn't measure enough of it, so Compy can't say {{game}} is back in its usual range yet.
evidence.driftRestoredOffAgain: Compy read it back on by {{restored}}, then noticed it off again on {{noticed}}. Compy doesn't count {{game}} sessions from {{until}} on as after it was back on.
evidence.recoveredDriftBack: Compy read that setting back on at {{restored}}, before the sessions that ran normally. That is consistent with that setting, but it doesn't prove it.
evidence.compyChangesRestore: Compy's count of changes that are on went from {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the ones that ran normally. That is what turning that setting back on would do.
evidence.recoveredCompyExplained: Compy's count of changes that are on went from {{from}} to {{to}} between the rough sessions and the normal ones, the same stretch in which that setting was read back on, so it isn't counted as another change.
evidence.whichNotRecorded: Which setting it was, and what changed it, isn't recorded.
evidence.whichNotLoaded: Compy couldn't read which setting it was just now. What changed it isn't recorded.
evidence.alreadyRunningScoped_one: Compy recorded what was running at the start of {{n}} of the {{of}} rough {{game}} sessions; {{name}} was already running in that one.
evidence.alreadyRunningScoped_other: Compy recorded what was running at the start of {{n}} of the {{of}} rough {{game}} sessions; {{name}} was already running in all {{n}}.
evidence.countChanged: Compy had {{from}} changes on in the last normal session and {{to}} in the first rough one.
evidence.hardwareChanged: The graphics card or memory Compy recorded is different.
evidence.powerPlanChanged: The power plan recorded on the two sessions is different.
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_one: {{count}} session ran normally on the new driver (on {{date}}).
evidence.normalOnNewDriver_other: {{count}} sessions ran normally on the new driver (the latest on {{date}}).
evidence.partialRoughOnOldDriver: A partly measured session on {{date}}, on the old driver, also looked rough.
evidence.crossGameConfounded: {{games}}'s rough sessions had other programs starting during them, or have no load numbers, so this can't point to the driver alone.
evidence.capChanged: The frame cap went from {{from}} to {{to}}.
evidence.installRecorded: Windows recorded the driver install on {{when}}.
evidence.installNotRecorded: Windows has no record of a graphics driver install in this period, though the driver version Compy saw changed (it saw the new version on {{when}}).
evidence.installAfterRough: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}, after the first rough session had started.
evidence.crossGameAfter: {{games}}'s rough sessions also came after the update.
evidence.updateMore_one: {{count}} more update was installed in the same period.
evidence.updateMore_other: {{count}} more updates were installed in the same period.
evidence.filesChanged: Steam says {{game}}'s files changed on {{when}}. That can be an update, a file verification or added content.
evidence.installedAndStarted: {{name}} was installed on {{day}} and also started during the rough sessions.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_one: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver install on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.otherDriverInstalled_other: Windows recorded {{count}} {{classes}} driver installs, the first on {{when}}, and nothing else Compy found lines up with the timing.
evidence.reinstallSameVersion: Windows recorded the same driver version being installed again on {{when}}.
evidence.installPriorUnknown: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}; the version before it isn't known.
evidence.recoveredSameDriver: {{game}} ran normally again on the same driver ({{version}}). That weakens the driver as the reason, though some driver problems come and go.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChange: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} on {{when}}.
evidence.recoveredAfterDriverChangeSeen: It recovered after the driver changed to {{version}} (Compy first saw it on {{when}}).
evidence.recoveredQuiet: Compy saw no build or encoding program start, and the rest of your PC was quiet ({{pct}}% CPU used by other programs) in the sessions that ran normally. That is consistent with background programs, but Compy can't see programs that were already running.
evidence.roughLoadNotRecorded: Compy didn't record how busy the PC was in every rough session, so this comparison is one-sided.

evidence.recoveredRamLower: Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable when it ran normally, against {{roughGb}} GB in the rough sessions. That is consistent with memory.

fix.title: How to fix it

gpuDriver.step1: Press Windows + X and open Device Manager.
gpuDriver.step2: Open Display adapters, double-click your graphics card, then open the Driver tab.
gpuDriver.step3: If "Roll Back Driver" can be clicked, click it and restart. Your previous version was {{from}}.
gpuDriver.step4: If it's greyed out, download {{from}} from the graphics maker's previous-drivers page, run it, and choose the clean install option.
gpuDriver.step5: Then play {{game}} for one session and press Something's wrong again. Compy will say whether that session was rough or in the usual range, or that it can't tell yet. It needs two sessions in the usual range before it says {{game}} is back to normal.
gpuDriver.stepBack: Compy read {{from}} again by {{back}}. Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

backgroundLoad.step1NoNames: Close other programs, especially anything building, recording or downloading, while you play.
backgroundLoad.step2: Play {{game}} once with them closed, then press Something's wrong again.
backgroundLoad.stepProgram: Close {{name}} before you play, then play once and press Something's wrong again.
backgroundLoad.stepNotOpen_one: Compy didn't see {{name}} open when your last {{game}} session started. Play {{game}} once more the same way, then press Something's wrong again.
backgroundLoad.stepNotOpen_other: Compy didn't see {{name}} open when your last {{game}} session started. Play {{game}} once more the same way, then press Something's wrong again.

memoryPressure.step1: Close browser tabs and launchers before you play. Memory peaked at {{peakGb}} of {{totalGb}} GB usable.
memoryPressure.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

settingDrift.step1: Check the setting in Windows, and any Windows setting you changed yourself.
settingDrift.stepTurnOn: Turn it back on in {{room}}, where Compy asks you to confirm first.
settingDrift.stepTurnOnHere: Turn it back on here or in {{room}}. Compy asks you to confirm first and saves how it was, so you can undo it in {{room}}.
settingDrift.turnedOn: You turned “{{title}}” back on with Compy at {{when}}. Play {{game}} once, for at least 10 minutes, then press Something's wrong again.
settingDrift.turnedOnNoTime: You turned “{{title}}” back on with Compy. Play {{game}} once, for at least 10 minutes, then press Something's wrong again.
settingDrift.secondChange: You turned on “{{other}}” earlier from this card. If you change two things before you play, Compy can't tell which one made the difference.
settingDrift.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.
settingDrift.stepBackOn: Compy read it back on by {{restored}}. Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

compyChange.step1: Open {{room}} and look at the changes Compy has on. Undo the newest one.
compyChange.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.
compyChange.undoExtra: Compy recorded this change between your last normal {{game}} session and the first rough one. Undoing it puts back what Compy saved before it; it doesn't tell Compy whether this change was the reason.
compyChange.undone: Undone on {{date}}: “{{title}}”. Play {{game}} once the way you usually do, then press Something's wrong again.
compyChange.several_other: Compy recorded changes to {{count}} settings in that time: {{titles}}. To check them one at a time, undo one in Test → Applied & history, then play once before undoing the next.
compyChange.noUndoHere: Compy doesn't offer to undo “{{title}}” from this card. You can see it, and undo it if you choose, in Test → Applied & history.
compyChange.changedSinceDrawn: This changed since the card was drawn, so Compy didn't undo anything. Press Something's wrong again.
compyChange.trialRunning: A Trial is running, or Compy can't tell whether one is, so it didn't undo anything. Check Test, then press Something's wrong again.
compyChange.listUnread: Compy couldn't read its change list just now, so it didn't undo anything. Press Something's wrong again.

fix.none: Compy has no change to offer for this. Check it in Windows, then play once more.

frameCapChange.step1: Set the frame cap in the game or in your graphics settings back to what it was ({{from}}), or leave it as it is.
frameCapChange.step2: Play {{game}} a few times. Compy only compares like with like, and needs 3 normal sessions with the new setting.

windowsUpdate.step1: Open Settings, then Windows Update, then Update history to see what was installed and when.
windowsUpdate.stepUninstall: If you want to test it, Update history has "Uninstall updates". You can remove {{kb}} there and restart. That's your choice; Compy won't do it for you.
windowsUpdate.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

gameFiles.step1: Check {{game}}'s patch notes for what changed around that date.
gameFiles.step2: In Steam, right-click {{game}}, open Properties, then Installed Files, and choose Verify integrity of game files.
gameFiles.step3: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

programInstalled.step1: Close {{names}} while you play, or uninstall it if you don't need it.
programInstalled.step2: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

graphicsMod.step1: Check {{name}}'s own page for a newer version.
graphicsMod.step2: To test without it, move its files out of the game folder (or use its own uninstall), play once, and press Something's wrong again.

gpuHotter.step1: Check that the card's fans spin up when you play, and look at the fans and heatsink for dust.
gpuHotter.step2: Check that the case has clear airflow in and out, and look at the card's fan curve in its own tool (it may be set too low).
gpuHotter.step3: Play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.

card.notProven: Compy can't prove this until you try the fix and play again.

card.somethingElse: Something else? Answer a few questions

why.crossGame: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too. The other changes don't line up with every rough session.
why.tie: Two changes line up equally. Start with the one that's easier to undo.
why.crossGameLead: It changed just before {{game}} got rough, and {{games}} got rough right after it too.

cantTell.crash: Crashes have their own page for now. Open Problems to see what Windows recorded.
cantTell.noGame: Compy hasn't recorded {{game}} yet. Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.noSessions: Compy hasn't recorded any games yet. Compy can measure a game while you play. It needs about 3 sessions of the same game before it can compare. Start a capture in Live, play as usual, and press Check again here afterwards.
cantTell.partialRough: Compy only measured part of your last {{game}} session ({{percent}}%), and what it saw looked rough. Play once more with Compy running.
cantTell.frameCap: Your frame cap changed, or Compy can't read it, between your earlier {{game}} sessions and the newest one, so it won't compare them.
cantTell.backToNormal: Compy can't tell yet whether {{game}} is back to normal. Play once more.
cantTell.oneClear: One session since has run the way {{game}} usually does. Compy says more after another one.
cantTell.recoveryCap: {{game}}'s frame cap is different now, so Compy can't compare these sessions with the earlier ones.

measuredOnce.title: {{game}}'s last session ran in its usual range
measuredOnce.numbers: Its dips stayed at about {{beforePct}}% of its average before, fell to about {{roughPct}}% while it was rough, and were at about {{nowPct}}% on {{date}}.
measuredOnce.notYet: One session can't show why it ran better, and it doesn't make any change below more likely. Play {{game}} once more and press Something's wrong again.
measuredOnce.cantAttribute: More than one change was recorded between the rough sessions and this one, so Compy can't tell which one mattered.

nothingChanged.title: Compy measured the problem, but nothing it records changed before it
nothingChanged.next: Play one more session, then press Something's wrong again. Compy will say whether it was rough or in the usual range, or that it can't tell yet.

footer: Compy lists what changed before the problem. It doesn't claim to know the cause.

notSeparable.title: Compy can't tell which of these it is yet
notSeparable.next: To find out: play one session of {{game}} with nothing else running, then press Something's wrong again. Compy will say whether that session was rough or in the usual range, or that it can't tell yet.
notSeparable.nextOther: Play {{game}} once more. Compy may still not be able to tell these apart.

seen.settingMoved: Compy noticed a setting it watches off on {{noticed}}.
seen.settingMovedBack: Compy noticed a setting it watches off on {{noticed}}. It was back on by {{restored}}.
seen.settingMovedReadAgain: Compy noticed a setting it watches had changed on {{noticed}}. It read as before again by {{restored}}.
seen.updatesMinor: {{n}} security definition and {{m}} app updates (listed for completeness).
seen.programsInstalledMore: {{count}} programs were installed on {{day}}: {{names}} and {{more}} more.
seen.programsNone: No program with a recorded install date was installed in this period.
seen.otherDrivers_one: {{count}} other driver was installed in this period ({{classes}}).
seen.otherDrivers_other: {{count}} other drivers were installed in this period ({{classes}}).
seen.driverInstallSameStamp: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}}, but the driver version on your sessions didn't change.
seen.driverOtherInstall: Windows recorded a graphics driver install on {{when}} for a different version than the one your rough sessions ran on.
seen.modSettingsOnly: {{game}}'s folder contains a settings or data file from {{name}}; Compy can't tell whether the mod itself is installed.
seen.gameCrashSignature: All the crashes Compy could read stopped in the same file ({{module}}), and some happened before {{what}}, so that change can't be the whole story for them.
seen.crashBeforeWhat: the earliest change with an exact time that Compy found between your last normal session and the rough ones ({{date}}, {{kind}})
seen.crashBeforeWhatNoKind: the earliest change with an exact time that Compy found between your last normal session and the rough ones ({{date}})
seen.crashBeforeWindowsOnly: a change Windows recorded between your last normal session and the rough ones ({{date}})
seen.gpuTemp_one: Graphics card temperature peaked at {{rough}}°C in the rough session; in normal sessions it typically peaks around {{base}}°C.
seen.gpuTemp_other: Graphics card temperature peaked at {{rough}}°C in the rough sessions (the highest of them); in normal sessions it typically peaks around {{base}}°C.
seen.gameCrashesPartial_one: Windows' crash records that Compy could read show {{game}} closing unexpectedly at least once, on {{since}}.
seen.gameCrashesPartial_other: Windows' crash records that Compy could read show {{game}} closing unexpectedly at least {{count}} times. The oldest of these is from {{since}}.
seen.crashesVersions: These crashes are across {{n}} versions of the game.
seen.startsDropped: Compy stopped listing program starts partway through ({{n}} more were not listed).
seen.startsSkipped: Compy didn't list some program starts that happened at the same moment.
seen.sittingMerged_one: Once, the game closed and was opened again within 10 minutes. Compy counted those launches as one session.
seen.sittingMerged_other: {{count}} times, the game closed and was opened again within 10 minutes. Compy counted each of those as one session.

limit.notSteam: Compy couldn't match {{game}} to a Steam install, so it can't see when it was updated.
limit.classes: Compy reads graphics, audio, network and chipset driver installs only, not other drivers.
limit.noInstallDate: Compy can't see Store apps, or programs that don't record an install date ({{n}} here).

why.accessDenied: Windows needs administrator rights to show that log
why.logEmpty: that Windows log is empty or switched off
why.logMissing: this PC has no such Windows log
why.recordsUnreadable: Windows returned {{n}} records Compy couldn't read
why.registry: the list of installed programs couldn't be opened
why.steamNoRecord: Steam has no record of this game
why.steamNoTime: Steam's record has no update time
why.notRead: Compy didn't look it up for this answer
why.tookTooLong: reading took too long, so Compy went on without it
why.noWindow: there was no period to look at
why.partialTimedOut: reading ran out of time, so only the newest records were read
why.partialRowCap: the log holds more records than Compy reads, so older ones are missing
why.partialOutputCapped: the log was too long to read in full
why.partialSteamLibraries: {{n}} Steam library folders couldn't be read
why.partialCoverage: Windows' log only goes back to {{from}}

verdict.likely: One change lines up best with what happened. It's listed first.
verdict.possible: A change lines up with when it started, but Compy can't prove it.
verdict.possibleMeasured: Compy measured something different during the rough session, but can't tie it to when the problem started.
verdict.testOne: Try one thing at a time; if you change two things before the next session, Compy can't tell which one mattered.

next.likely: Try the steps under the first one, play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again.
next.possible: Check it, play {{game}} once, then press Something's wrong again. Compy will say whether that session was rough or in the usual range, or that it can't tell yet. It needs two sessions in the usual range before it says {{game}} is back to normal.

recovered.title: {{game}}'s last two sessions ran the way it usually does
recovered.numbers: Its dips stayed at about {{beforePct}}% of its average before, fell to about {{roughPct}}% while it was rough, and are at about {{nowPct}}% now.
recovered.pointsTo: Of the changes listed, only one is still standing after these sessions: {{what}}. That matches the timing, but two sessions can't show why it ran better.
recovered.settingBack_one: Compy read the setting back on before those two sessions. Among the changes Compy keeps track of (drivers, Windows updates, game files, installed programs), it found no other one in that stretch. That's consistent with the setting being what mattered, but it doesn't prove it.
recovered.settingBack_other: Compy read those settings back on before those two sessions. Among the changes Compy keeps track of (drivers, Windows updates, game files, installed programs), it found no other one in that stretch. That's consistent with those settings being what mattered, but it doesn't prove it.
recovered.betweenCantTell: More than one change was recorded in that stretch, so Compy can't tell which one mattered.
recovered.nothing: Compy can't narrow it down from this recovery.
recovered.next: If it runs rough again, press Something's wrong again and Compy will say whether that session was rough or in the usual range, or that it can't tell yet.
recovered.notProven: This is what the recorded sessions show. It doesn't prove why it got better.

sinceLast.title: Since the last check
sinceLast.newSessions_other: {{count}} new {{game}} sessions were recorded, the latest on {{date}}.
sinceLast.newSessionsCapped: At least one new {{game}} session was recorded, the latest on {{date}}.
sinceLast.fewer: Fewer {{game}} sessions are recorded than at the last check.
sinceLast.lessRead: This time Compy couldn't read everything it read last time, so a change may not show here.
sinceLast.unchangedNoNew: No new {{game}} session was recorded and nothing in the answer changed. Play {{game}} once, then press Check again.
sinceLast.otherGame: This answer is about {{game}}; the last one was about {{prev}}.

stateLabel.once: one session in its usual range
stateLabel.recovered: two sessions in its usual range
